title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: Claim δΦ* = δΦ \ Φ_red needs care at the ends of L. If t1 is minimal in L, t1 ∈ Φ and I_{t1,t2} ∈ Φ, then ord(t1,Φ) = 1, so t1 is not redundant. Yet no stratum of Φ* contains t1 as point or endpoint, so t1 ∉ δΦ*. Such points (presumably the 'sommets-bord impropres' of the digression) must also be removed, or redundancy redefined to include them. The digression on five vertex types suggests Grothendieck was aware of this subtlety.

ideas.what: Complement of a polyfigure inside the maximal polyfigure of its flag, Φ* = Φ̂ \ Φ, and the double complement Φ** as erasure of redundant vertices by composing adjacent intervals
ideas.modern_name: regularization / coarsening of a stratification of a 1-dimensional ordered set; analogue of regular-open (int∘cl) operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (regular open sets: Stone/Kuratowski; coarsest stratification: standard in o-minimal/PL geometry)

ideas.what: Classification of vertices of a μ̂-polygon into five types (isolated, proper/improper boundary, proper/improper interior = redundant)
ideas.modern_name: vertex types in a 1-dimensional cell complex / stratified segment

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary combinatorial lemma about complements of finite sets of points and intervals on a line, preparatory to a later key result. Correct up to an edge case. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
